_doc: SKEPTIC pre-registration, written BEFORE any deck was generated or run in this workdir. Role: re-run, do not read. Police Track 1's fastest functional point, re-derive Track 2's crossover independently, re-run Track 3's QAL->sync level test, and COMPOSE them. Speed is the primary metric; energy is reported and gates nothing.
cache: /tmp/claude-1001/-usr-local-src/4921ad0c-f17b-4b84-986a-5917c9ebd2a6/scratchpad/vae_cache_skept2 (seeded from vae_cache_lsweep + vae_cache_boundT3; geometry-only reuse, no results reused)

instrument_gates_PRE_STATED.I0_committed_deck: The COMMITTED deck qal/swsweep/sw_tg15p_z.cir, re-run byte-identical in my workdir under MY cache, must reproduce the committed .mt0 headlines VBPK / VBEND / VAEND / IPK / IZ to rel < 1e-6. Separates my toolchain from my arithmetic.
instrument_gates_PRE_STATED.I1_my_generator: My OWN independently written deck generator at the anchor point (L=277.8 nH, TG 5/10 um + 1 um park, dV=1.0, RS=10, CA=35.979 fF) must reproduce the committed true zero 266.755 ps to within 1.5 ps and VBEND 0.6758936 to within 0.5%.
instrument_gates_PRE_STATED.I2_lag_claim: Track 1 claims a CONSTANT 1.0 ps lag in this Xyce build's '.measure tran X FIND expr AT=T'. I test it independently: one deck, print step <= 0.02 ps, FIND at several T, compared against the .prn value at T. PASS = lag reproduced to within 0.1 ps. If it is NOT 1.0 ps, every Track 1 number that used LAG_PS=1.0 is suspect and I say so.
instrument_gates_PRE_STATED.I3_waveform_only: Every SPEED number I report is taken from the .prn waveform by my own extractor, never from .measure alone, so no speed claim can depend on the lag at all.

a_rerun_acceptance_PRE_STATED.points: (1) Track 1's HEADLINE fastest functional point L=15 nH, TG 10/20 um + 2 um park, dV=1.2. (2) One MID-SWEEP point: L=45 nH, TG 5/10 + 1 um park, dV=1.0 -- Track 1's 'last functional at W=15/dV=1.0', i.e. the load-bearing boundary row.
a_rerun_acceptance_PRE_STATED.reproduction: REPRODUCED iff my t_hop is within 3% and my VBEND / VA_open within 1% (absolute 0.01 V) of Track 1's reported values (headline t_hop 65.495 ps, VBEND 0.71382, VA_open 0.12768, t_level 123.443 / 115.571 ps; mid t_hop 105.701 ps, VBEND 0.6298, VA_open 0.1461). Outside that = NOT REPRODUCED and reported as such.
a_rerun_acceptance_PRE_STATED.per_cell_settling_POLICE: All 8 cells individually, at BOTH checkpoints, from the waveform: (i) at the switch-open instant, (ii) at end of the 500 ps tail. lo-input cell s = V(o)/V(bkb); hi-input cell s = 1 - V(o)/V(bkb). A speed claim resting on a partly-settled bank is vacuous. I additionally require an ABSOLUTE margin test that Track 1 did NOT state: every lo cell output must exceed, and every hi cell output must stay below, the MEASURED DC trip point of the downstream receiver I build in (c). A bank whose outputs straddle no usable trip point is not computing, whatever its percentage settling says.
a_rerun_acceptance_PRE_STATED.t_level: t_level = max(t_hop, t_valid90) with t_valid90 = first time after switch close at which ALL 8 cells are simultaneously within 90% (lo) / within 10% (hi) of the INSTANTANEOUS rail and stay there to end of run. Reported alongside t_settle90 (against the FINAL rail). Verdict on the conservative of the two.

c_boundary_acceptance_PRE_STATED.test: QAL bank level -> standard sync gate, re-run by me. DC transfer curves (my own .DC sweep) of: (i) the campaign's standard generic inverter 1.12u/0.74u @1.2 V, (ii) Track 3's 'cell K' 0.15u/1.48u @0.9 V, (iii) 0.15u/1.48u @1.2 V. Extract trip point and static contention current vs input level.
c_boundary_acceptance_PRE_STATED.range_requirement: PASS requires margin across a RANGE, not at the nominal point: the receiver must resolve correctly for delivered levels spanning the family's measured spread, 0.55 V to 0.85 V, with >= 100 mV of margin between the QAL high level and the trip point AND between the trip point and the QAL low level. Nominal-point-only success is recorded as FAILS-ON-RANGE.
c_boundary_acceptance_PRE_STATED.driver_realism: Track 3 drove its receiver from an IDEAL PWL source. I additionally drive it from the REAL QAL cell output inside the real hop deck, because the real driver is a 1.12u/0.74u inverter on a 0.68-0.71 V resonant rail and must also supply the receiver's static contention current. If the two differ materially, the PWL result is an idealisation and I say so.

d_composition_acceptance_PRE_STATED.test: Track 1's FASTEST FUNCTIONAL point with Track 3's boundary attached: one receiver per cell output (8 receivers) on the real hop deck, at L=15 nH / W=30 um / dV=1.2.
d_composition_acceptance_PRE_STATED.joint_pass: JOINT PASS requires ALL of: (i) all 8 cells still >= 90% settled at the end checkpoint; (ii) VBEND >= 0.60 V ABSOLUTE (Track 1's own pre-registered C3 device-Vt floor, not a fraction of dV); (iii) VA_open <= 0.1478 (Track 1's C2 transfer completeness); (iv) every receiver resolves to the correct logic value, crossing 50% of its own output rail, inside the QAL valid window. FAILING ANY ONE = the composition does not hold and the tracks' separate passes were obtained by zeroing each other's term.
d_composition_acceptance_PRE_STATED.t_level_with_boundary: t_level_b = max(t_hop, t_valid90, t_receiver_resolve). This, not t_hop, is the quantity that can be compared to a CMOS logic level.
d_composition_acceptance_PRE_STATED.switch_widening_crosscheck: Does the switch widening Track 1 needed (15 -> 30 um at dV=1.2) change Track 3's answer? Run the same composition at W=15 um, same L and dV, and report whether the boundary verdict flips.

b_crossover_recheck_PRE_STATED.method: Re-derive the crossover arithmetic myself from the definition throughput_QAL > throughput_CMOS <=> n_beat * t_beat_QAL < d * t_level_CMOS + t_reg, independently of Track 2's script. Verify Track 2's flop-overhead provenance: if CQ/setup came from liberty, check the liberty tables directly and check OpenSTA's interpolation, and flag them against the record's finding that liberty internal-power is 1.5-3.7x low and its th22 entry was wrong.
b_crossover_recheck_PRE_STATED.power_vs_timing: The record's liberty indictment is about INTERNAL POWER, not delay. I will state explicitly whether it transfers to the timing tables or not, rather than assuming either way.

comparators_PRE_STATED.cmos_logic_level: 92.8 ps = sha_slice MEASURED comb path 928.1 ps / mapped depth 10 (the record's own figure). Combinational, NO flop overhead.
comparators_PRE_STATED.cmos_inverter: 34.81 ps committed SG13G2 inverter anchor (1.2 V, 2 fF, full cycle).
comparators_PRE_STATED.faster_means: QAL is FASTER than a CMOS logic level iff t_level (or t_level_b where a boundary is attached) < 92.8 ps. t_hop alone is NOT the comparator and t_hop/8 will not be claimed as a speed win.

declared_limits_PRE_STATED: sg13lv_compat.sp zeroes ad/as/pd/ps, so junction capacitance is ABSENT: every capacitance, charge, energy and delay is a LOWER BOUND / optimistic, worst at wide-switch fast points.
Gate drive of the transfer switch is an ideal PWL source with a 2 ps edge; a 30-60 um TG gate cannot be driven that fast, so the driver's own delay is EXCLUDED.
The 8 metered cells have DC inputs: this is a RAIL-ARRIVAL test, not logic evaluation. Inherited from the committed harness.
One hop, not a chain and not a pipeline. No multi-hop charge recovery, no register-tax claim is measured here.
Energy is reported; no energy verdict is claimed or overturned. The EXCLUSION verdict stands on its own ledger.
